title: Part Twenty-Six: Outside the Jar: Mary, Judas and Pistis Sophia

sections.brief: Gospel of Mary: Berlin Codex 8502 (Reinhardt, Cairo, Jan 1896; Till 1955), Greek fragments P.Ryl. 463 and P.Oxy. 3525, pp.1-6 and 11-14 missing; outline; teachings (sin, Son of Humanity within, 'lay down no rules', vision through the mind, ascent past the powers); Peter and Andrew vs Mary, Levi's defence; not named in any ancient condemnation (Decretum silent; Epiphanius on a different 'Questions of Mary'); Gregory I Homily 33 c.591 conflation, 1969 calendar, 3 June 2016 feast; Ordinatio Sacerdotalis 1994 and Petrocchi report 4 Dec 2025 on women's ordination. Figures: flow (soul's ascent); time (institution's record)

Gospel of Judas: Irenaeus AH I.31 c.180 and Epiphanius 374-377; Codex Tchacos provenance (Maghagha 1970s to NatGeo 6 April 2006; radiocarbon 220-340); contents; outline (mocked eucharist, temple vision, Sethian cosmology, 'the man that clothes me'); attack on the twelve and their sacrifice (Pagels and King's protest reading); hero vs demon (DeConick 2007) readings; 2006 responses: Benedict XVI 13 April and 18 October 2006, Rowan Williams. Figures: time (text history); compare (two readings)

Pistis Sophia: Askew Codex (Askew 1772, British Museum 1785, BL Add MS 5114), Schwartze 1851, Mead 1896/1921; outline of four books; Sophia's fall from the thirteenth aeon, repentances interpreted through Psalms and Odes, restoration; Book Three's renunciation code (counter to 'no commandments'); Mary prominent, Peter's complaints (ch.36, ch.72); Bruce Codex and the Books of Jeu (James Bruce c.1769); no ancient condemnation on record; labelled interpretation (fall as ascent map); close on what the canon kept about Mary. Figures: flow (Sophia myth)
